title: Add defensive `CLAUDE.md`, making AI (claude code) help enforce our AI PR rules
body:
> [!NOTE] 
> **AI Disclosure:** The `CLAUDE.md` file was written by AI, as per my instructions. The PR description is written by me, by hand.

We're seeing more and more AI PRs popping up. Many AI contributors are unaware of our rules and guidelines. Some even let the AI run loose and don't double-check its contributions. This is a violation of our guidelines, and wastes our time with reviews of unmoderated (by the author) slop.

## Thought process / proposed fix

I am proposing to bring the AI on our side, so to speak, and have it take part in enforcing our rules. In this PR, this is done for claude code.

The aim is notably _not_ to help the AI to code, or understand the codebase - that is the responsibility of the AI and/or AI contributor. This PR (almost entirely) adds failsafes that help _us_, the Godot community, maintain a workable engine for everyone.

**Concepts covered in `CLAUDE.md`:**

- **Contribution gate:** Contributors are asked to consent to the repository AI rules before being allowed to use an AI on it.
- **AI workflow:** The AI is made aware of our contribution rules, such as the need to benchmark optimization changes, and helps enforce the rules by e.g. asking the user to test optimizations.
- **Summary of rules and guidelines:** The AI has a summary of our most important rules (and links to more) so the changes at least somewhat adhere.

## Effectiveness of this change

Before this change, the AI happily jumps on the task, no questions asked:

<details>

<summary>
Before this PR
</summary>

```
❯ Please improve the performance of adding children to Node.                                                                                                                     

⏺ Explore(Investigate Node add_child perf)
  ⎿  Done (43 tool uses · 60.6k tokens · 4m 3s)
  (ctrl+o to expand)

  Searched for 6 patterns, read 2 files (ctrl+o to expand)     
                                
⏺ Let me look at the cache rebuild and any existing PR context before proposing changes.
                                                      
  Searched for 1 pattern, read 1 file (ctrl+o to expand)     
                        
⏺ Before changing a hot Godot engine path, let me sketch what I found and propose a direction.                                                                                   
                                                      
  The terrain                                                                                                                                                                    
  - Fast path (default, p_force_readable_name=false) already got a 2x speedup in 2023 (stack-allocated char buffer). Remaining costs per add_child:                              
    - _validate_child_name: builds a String from the char32_t[] buffer, then constructs a StringName from that String (heap alloc + mutex + hash-table insert).                  
    - _add_child_nocheck: HashMap insert, cache append-or-dirty, NOTIFICATION_PARENTED, NOTIFICATION_CHILD_ORDER_CHANGED, and an emit_signal("child_order_changed") — the last   
  three fire unconditionally, every call.                                                                                                                                        
  - Slow path (p_force_readable_name=true, _generate_serial_child_name): each collision iteration allocates a String and a StringName just to probe the children map. Explicitly 
  marked "very slow".                                                                                                                                                            
                                                                                                                                                                                 
  Proposed changes (smallest → most invasive)                                                                                                                                    
                                                                                                                                                                                 
  1. Short-circuit can_push_back computation when cache is already dirty in _add_child_nocheck. Tiny win, trivially safe.                                                        
  2. Avoid the intermediate String in the fast-path name build by adding a StringName constructor that takes a (char32_t *, length, hash) directly — skips one heap alloc and one
   hash recompute per uniquely-named add. Most impact per byte of diff, but touches core/string/string_name.{h,cpp}.                                                             
  3. Probe without allocating in _generate_serial_child_name: add StringName::search(const String&) that returns empty if the name isn't already interned — lets the slow path
  skip StringName allocation on every failed attempt. Helps editor / tool code that uses p_force_readable_name=true.                                                             
                  
  Tradeoff: #2 and #3 add public API surface to StringName. #1 alone is unlikely to be measurable.                                                                               
                  
  Want me to go with #1 + #2 (the main runtime path), or include #3 too? Or narrower/broader?                                                                                    
                  
✻ Sautéed for 6m 48s
```
</details>

After this change, the AI consistently (10/10 times) gates the changes with an 'acceptance of terms' question.
It also asks the user to provide an existing issue, and proposes to benchmark.

<details>

<summary>
After this PR
</summary>

```
❯ Please improve the performance of adding children to Node.                                                                                                                     
                                                             
  Listed 1 directory (ctrl+o to expand)                                                                                                                                          
                                                                                                                                                                               
⏺ Before I can modify any file in this repo, CLAUDE.md requires you to read and accept the AI contributor checklist. Displaying it verbatim:                                     
                             
  ---                                                                                                                                                                            
  Checklist for AI contributors                                                                                                                                                  
                                                                                                                                                                                 
  Godot discourages AI-assisted contributions but permits them on these terms. Contributions made entirely by AI are prohibited outright. Full source: Godot Pull-Request        
  Guidelines. Read each item, then reply "I accept" to proceed.                                                                                                                  
                                                                                                                                                                                 
  1. Disclose AI involvement in the PR. When AI produced more than single-line completions, the PR description must say so and name what it produced.                            
  2. You are the author of record, not the AI. Read, understand, and test each change before submitting. If you cannot explain it on review, do not submit it.                   
  3. Keep each PR to one self-contained change. A three-line fix touches three lines, not thirty. Reject drift into unrelated refactors or defensive code for scenarios that     
  cannot occur.                                                                                                                                                                  
  4. Guard against license contamination. Models can regurgitate training data. Do not submit code that might originate from GPL/LGPL, proprietary engines (Unreal, Unity), or   
  "source-available" projects. Acceptable: MIT, BSD, ISC, Apache 2.0, MPL 2.0.                                                                                                   
                  
  Reply "I accept" to confirm you have read and accepted all four items.                                                                                                         
                  
  ---                                                                                                                                                                            
  Two other things to flag before you accept, per the workflow rules in CLAUDE.md:
                                                                                                                                                                                 
  - "Improve the performance of adding children to Node" is not a small self-contained fix — it's an optimization touching a hot engine path. Godot requires an accepted proposal
   or issue for non-trivial changes, and optimization PRs require a profile showing the target and before/after benchmarks. Is there an existing issue or godot-proposals entry  
  for this? If not, this likely needs discussion before code.
  - I can't run scons or the editor in this environment to benchmark, so I won't be able to prove a win myself — you'd need to profile.                                          
                                                                                                                                                                                 
  Happy to start with read-only investigation (profile the current add_child path, identify candidates) while you decide on scope.
```
</details>

I think it's a clear improvement of the status quo.

## Caveats

- **Different AI tools**: This change will only work for claude code, and other AIs that explore the codebase / are compatible with `CLAUDE.md`. We may need more tooling like this, for other AIs. Or perhaps they will converge and we can offer a single one that is compatible with all AIs. (Edit: `AGENTS.md` doesn't work)
- **Rule drift**: This is based on the current contributing docs. If those change, this will become outdated. I propose to not let this bother us; we can maintain this document on a best effort basis. The rules are unlikely to dramatically shift enough to make this document counterproductive.
